what_happened: A step to change agent limits had two parts: raise the ceiling, and record plan group sizes. It failed twice. Both times the failure was in recording group sizes on the one-at-a-time path, and that blocked the simple ceiling change. The the person running Athena split it into two requests and spelled out the split by hand. No job id is attached.
cause: Athena accepts a request that bundles a simple config change with a separable code change, and nothing checks whether the parts can succeed independently. A failure in the harder part rejects the whole job, so a retry repeats the same bundle. The group-size recording also touches a core flow with a serial path that differs from the parallel one. Nothing splits a job after a repeated failure, so the the person running Athena does it by hand.
prevention: When a job fails twice on the same part, Athena should split the request automatically. It should queue the parts that do not depend on the failing part (here the ceiling raise) as separate jobs, and re-ask the failing part on its own with the failure finding. The reader or planner should also flag at admission that a request mixes a config-only change with a code change that adds recording in a core flow, and propose one job per change. The recording job's plan must cover the default one-at-a-time path.
proposed_request: Raise the agent-limit ceiling in athena.toml as its own job. Keep the change to the limit value and any tests that read it. Make sure the job-level budget still covers the sum of the stage caps. Do not record plan group sizes in this job. Then, as a separate follow-up job, record plan group sizes. It must give correct values on both the default one-at-a-time path (max_concurrency = 1) and the parallel path. Include a test for each path, and note what the two earlier failed attempts hit on the one-at-a-time path.
